constraint_decided_it: P43 has dimension is declared E70 Thing -> E54 Dimension, and E73 Information Object is an E70 (E73 < E90 < E28 < E71 < E70; the E73 dossier lists P43 among its applicable properties). A rejected E54 for the bootstrap values by reasoning from O12 has dimension (S15 -> E54), a CRMsci property whose domain simply is not the one in play, and so concluded the tree statistics have 'no home in the model beyond an opaque string'. P43's own scope note answers the case directly: 'Knowledge about an instance of E54 Dimension need not be the result of a measurement; it may be the result of evaluating data or other information, which should be documented as an instance of E13 Attribute Assignment.' A ruled out the construct the CRM actually prescribes on a constraint that does not apply.
better_modelling: Fish specimen: E20 Biological Object. Tissue extraction: CRMsci S2 Sample Taking producing an S13 Sample (A's note that CRMsci has no such class is false; both resolve in this corpus). Sequencing: not E16/S21 Measurement -- E16's scope note redirects 'determining properties of an instance of E90 Symbolic Object' to E13 Attribute Assignment, with P16 used specific object naming the E18 carrier used as empirical basis; in CRMsci the exact fit is S4 Single Observation with O8 observed the specimen and O16 observed value (S4 -> E1) carrying the sequence, since S21's result property O39 observed dimension ranges over E54 and a nucleotide string is not an E54. The sequence: E73 Information Object / E90 Symbolic Object, P190 has symbolic content if the string is to live in the KB, P1 is identified by the E42 accession number (shortcut for P140i / E15 Identifier Assignment / P37 assigned, the external database's activity). The phylogenetic tree: E73 Information Object (its scope note names 'data sets ... algorithm or mathematical formulae, that have an objectively recognizable structure and are documented as single units'), produced by an E13 Attribute Assignment / E65 Creation that P16 used the sequence. Bootstrap support: E54 Dimension attached to the tree by P43 has dimension, with P2 has type 'bootstrap support' (E54's scope note: the quantity may be 'theoretically derived' and 'the method of determination should be expressed using the property P2 has type'), P90 has value, P91 has unit. So the answer to the curator is: the CRM does give the tree statistics a first-class, queryable home -- just on the tree, not on the fish.
reasoning: Both reach the same top-line advice (document the sequencing, hold the accession number, do not become the master copy), so the separation is entirely in the constraint work. A is wrong twice over: it denies E54 Dimension to the bootstrap values by invoking O12 (S15 -> E54) instead of the applicable P43 (E70 -> E54), whose scope note explicitly covers non-measured, evaluated dimensions via E13 Attribute Assignment; and it types the sequencing as S21 Measurement while quoting the very E16 scope note that redirects determination of E90 Symbolic Object properties to E13 Attribute Assignment, leaving the sequence itself with no class at all (S21's O39 observed dimension ranges over E54, so it cannot hold a nucleotide string). Its claim that 'no class in the base model or in CRMsci represents a phylogenetic tree' is refuted by E73's own scope note, and its note that CRMsci offers no sample-taking step is refuted by S2 Sample Taking / S13 Sample. B's citations all verify against the sources -- t1736 is Issue 490 'how to model a file' and does weigh KB-internal P190 against an external guaranteed URL/DOI copy, t1444 is the 2021 e-vote reducing P39's range to E18, the Appendix migration note on E16's reduced scope exists, the Introduction > Objectives sentence 'it has not been optimised for implementation specific storage and processing factors' is verbatim, and the Clayton Herbarium BM000038850.JPG example is in both the E73 and E90 dossiers -- and its exclusion of E16 for the bootstrap values is exactly right. B is only suboptimal: it settles for P3 has note where P43 / E54 applies, and P3's scope note defines itself as the container for descriptions 'not ... expressed in terms of CIDOC CRM constructs', so it is the wrong choice whenever a construct exists; it also types the sequencing as a generic E7 Activity where E13 Attribute Assignment is prescribed, and wrongly asserts the corpus holds no CRMsci (S21, S4, S2, S13, O12 all resolve).
